prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished desktop website design comp, 1536x1024 landscape: a real web layout, edge to edge, no device frame, no browser chrome.

The FIRST attached image is the approved look and feel for this page: match its header, type, spacing, white cards, canary-yellow buttons and highlights, and above all its premium matte isometric miniature desk (pale wood desktop, green blotter, a small canary, an open brass birdcage, soft studio daylight, one contact shadow). The other attached images are the same site's built homepage: they confirm the header (script wordmark "Birdcar" at left; nav "How I work", "Selected work", "Writing" and a canary-yellow pill "Book a free Walkthrough →"), the pale daylight ground #edf3f0, near-black ink #0b141a, the heavy tight grotesk (Mona Sans) for all text, white pill tags, and canary yellow #f7c848 only on actions and highlights. Do NOT copy any reference's content beyond that style; do not paint invented words on props (no text on notebooks, book spines, or signs).

This page is "The Walkthrough": the booking page for a free, pitch-free, roughly one-hour conversation with Nick (Birdcar), a systems engineer who builds tools for established service businesses. Within three business days the visitor gets a written report they keep: what's happening, what I recommend, and where I'd start. New requirement for this page: the visitor qualifies themselves before reaching the calendar. The fit check uses these exact lines: "You have customers and people doing the work." / "One process takes too much chasing, copying, or remembering." / "I can talk to the people who do it." and the honest disqualifier "If I can't talk to the people doing the work, I'm not the right fit."

STRUCTURE, in reading order (a fit card on the desk: the calendar card asks three questions before it shows times):
1. Header, about 80px, as the reference.
2. First viewport, two columns. LEFT (x 80 to 690): headline about 64px, two lines: "An hour on the work. A report you can use." Paragraph at about 19px: "In a free Walkthrough, you spend about an hour showing me the work that's giving you trouble. Within three business days you get my recommendations in writing." One medium line: "The hour is about your work. If you want to talk about hiring me, you'll bring it up, not me." Below, the compact white report card from the reference titled "Your Walkthrough report" with three rows "What's happening", "What I recommend", "Where I'd start" (canary-yellow row), and a muted line "In writing within three business days. Yours to keep."
RIGHT (x 760 to 1460, y 110 to 900): the miniature desk from the reference with the white card standing on it in the same place as the calendar was, same size, 14px radius. But the card is in its first state, a fit check: title "Before you pick a time", a muted line "Three quick checks. It takes ten seconds.", then three rows, each with the line on the left and a pair of small pill toggles "Yes" / "Not yet" on the right; the first two rows show "Yes" selected in ink: "You have customers and people doing the work." "One process takes too much chasing, copying, or remembering." "I can talk to the people who do it." At the card's foot a canary-yellow button "Show me times →" and a small muted line "If I can't talk to the people doing the work, I'm not the right fit." Behind the fit card, slightly offset, the edge of the calendar card peeks out, showing it waits underneath. The canary perches on the card's top-left corner; the open brass birdcage at the right.
3. Bottom band (y 910 to 1024) on white: three numbered steps in a row "1 Check the fit." "2 Choose a time." "3 Keep the report."

ART DIRECTION: one dominant move, the fit card on the desk; everything else holds still. Premium, adult, precise. Not cute. No purple, no gradient orbs, no robots, no AI imagery, no stock photos, no prices, no fake metrics, no testimonials. Preserve all quoted words exactly. Treat it as a finished, shippable website.
